# Create the TrueNAS SCALE VM {#sec-vm}

Install TrueNAS onto a **virtual OS disk** first, with no HBA attached. Confirm it boots. Add passthrough in @sec-passthrough.

## Download the TrueNAS SCALE ISO

- Get the ISO from the [TrueNAS download page](https://www.truenas.com/download-truenas-scale/). Pick the current **stable** release — the page also lists a newer beta line and Nightlies, neither of which is appropriate for a first install.
- Verify the download against the checksum published next to it on that page:

```bash
sha256sum TrueNAS-SCALE-*.iso
```

- Get the ISO onto Proxmox storage. Either upload it through the UI (**Datacenter → *node* → local (or other storage) → ISO Images → Upload**), or pull it straight from the Proxmox shell into the storage's ISO directory:

```bash
wget -O /var/lib/vz/template/iso/TrueNAS-SCALE-latest.iso \
  https://download.sys.truenas.net/TrueNAS-SCALE-Goldeye/latest/TrueNAS-SCALE.iso
```

Replace the URL with the one from the download page — the codename (currently "Goldeye" for the 25.10 line) changes with each release. `local` is the default storage name for ISOs; use whatever storage you configured for ISO Images if it differs.

## Settings that matter

| Setting | Value |
|---------|--------|
| Machine | **q35** |
| BIOS | **OVMF (UEFI)** |
| CPU type | **host** |
| Cores | 4 or more |
| RAM | 16 GB minimum, ballooning **off** |
| SCSI controller (OS disk only) | VirtIO SCSI |
| OS disk | 16–32 GB on Proxmox SSD/NVMe |
| Network | VirtIO on `vmbr0` |
| Start at boot | Off until passthrough works |

q35 is required for real PCIe. i440fx only does legacy PCI.

## Example `qm create`

```bash
qm create 300 \
  --name truenas \
  --memory 16384 \
  --balloon 0 \
  --cores 4 \
  --cpu host \
  --bios ovmf \
  --machine q35 \
  --efidisk0 local-lvm:1,efitype=4m,pre-enrolled-keys=0 \
  --scsihw virtio-scsi-single \
  --scsi0 local-lvm:32,ssd=1 \
  --ide2 local:iso/TrueNAS-SCALE-latest.iso,media=cdrom \
  --boot order=ide2\;scsi0 \
  --net0 virtio,bridge=vmbr0 \
  --ostype l26
```

`--ide2 ...,media=cdrom` attaches the ISO downloaded above; swap in your actual filename. `--boot order=ide2;scsi0` boots the installer first, then falls back to the virtual disk.

Start the VM, open its **Console** in the Proxmox UI, and run through the TrueNAS SCALE installer onto the virtual disk (`scsi0`) — the only disk it should see at this point, since the HBA isn't attached yet. Once TrueNAS boots on its own from `scsi0`:

```bash
qm set 300 --boot order=scsi0
qm set 300 --ide2 none
```

This drops the ISO and returns the boot order to the virtual disk only, so the VM doesn't try to reinstall on every reboot.

::: {.callout-tip}
Keep the TrueNAS boot pool on the virtual disk. The HBA is only for the data pool. You can rebuild the VM and import the same pool later.
:::

## Or: use the Create VM wizard

Everything above maps directly onto Proxmox's **Create VM** wizard (top-right button), tab by tab:

| Wizard tab | Field | Set to |
|---|---|---|
| General | VM ID / Name | `300` / `truenas` |
| OS | ISO image | The TrueNAS ISO uploaded earlier |
| OS | Type / Version | Linux / 6.x - 2.6 Kernel |
| System | Machine | `q35` |
| System | BIOS | `OVMF (UEFI)` |
| System | Add EFI Disk | Checked, storage `local-lvm`, untick **Pre-Enroll keys** |
| Disks | Bus/Device | SCSI, storage `local-lvm`, size `32` GiB |
| Disks | SCSI Controller | `VirtIO SCSI single` |
| Disks | SSD emulation | Checked |
| CPU | Cores | `4` |
| CPU | Type | `host` |
| Memory | Memory (MiB) | `16384`, untick **Ballooning Device** |
| Network | Bridge / Model | `vmbr0` / `VirtIO (paravirtualized)` |
| Confirm | Start after created | Untick if you want to double-check settings first |

::: {.callout-note}
The wizard adds the CD-ROM and disk in the order you configured them, which usually puts the CD-ROM first already. Before starting the VM, confirm the boot order under **Hardware → Options → Boot Order**: the CD-ROM (ISO) should be above the SCSI disk, and the HBA must not be listed at all yet. This is the GUI equivalent of `--boot order=ide2;scsi0`.
:::

After install, do the CLI cleanup's GUI equivalent: open **Hardware**, select the **CD/DVD Drive**, and either detach the ISO or set it to "Do not use any media" — then revisit **Options → Boot Order** and drop the CD-ROM entry (or untick it) so only the SCSI disk remains.
